name: Inductive Miner (pm4py)
author: Promenade Team
description: Discovers a process tree with pm4py's inductive miner, and converts it to an accepting Petri net. Runs in Pyodide.

actions.label: Inductive Miner (pm4py)
actions.description: Discovers a process tree from a traditional event log with pm4py's IMf variant. The tree is sound and block-structured by construction, so it always replays; the noise threshold trades fitness for simplicity.

agent.whenToUse: The default choice for discovering a model from a case-centric log — unlike the Alpha Miner it tolerates noise and always yields a sound model.
agent.notFor: Object-centric logs (flatten first, or use an object-centric miner), and not a way to see infrequent behavior: raising noiseThreshold removes it.
examples: noiseThreshold 0.0 for the full behavior of a clean log
noiseThreshold 0.2 as a first readable model of a noisy real-world log
maxEvents to cap a large log while exploring

noiseThreshold.title: Noise threshold
noiseThreshold.description: Higher values simplify the model. Re-runs discovery; on a large log this is seconds, not milliseconds.

maxEvents.title: Event limit
maxEvents.description: A safety ceiling, not a normal control: the default covers any log this algorithm can comfortably mine in a browser tab, so almost no run should ever hit it. When one does, the result is flagged as truncated — lower this only to iterate faster on a huge log before committing to a full run. Changing it re-runs the expensive stage.

actions.label: Process tree → Petri net
actions.description: Converts a process tree into a behaviorally equivalent accepting Petri net, with an initial and a final marking.

agent.whenToUse: When a downstream action needs a Petri net — conformance checking and alignments take one, not a tree.
agent.notFor: Discovery. It adds no information; it only changes the representation.

recommends.reason: draws the process trees this plugin produces
